jp: 分[わ]からないこと{が|ga-existence}あれ{ば|ba-conditional}、先生[せんせい]{に|ni-target}聞[き]く{なり|nari-nari}友達[ともだち]{に|ni-target}相談[そうだん]する{なり|nari-nari}しなさい。
en: If there's anything you don't understand, ask your teacher or talk it over with a friend.
why: A pair of examples in the pattern Aなり Bなり offers either course of action as an option; the same なり must close both halves.

jp: 質問[しつもん]{が|ga-existence}あれ{ば|ba-conditional}、電話[でんわ]{なり|nari-nari}メール{なり|nari-nari}{で|de-means}ご連絡[れんらく]ください。
en: If you have a question, please contact us by phone or by e-mail, whichever you prefer.
why: Aなり Bなり names two acceptable options; after a first なり the pair is completed by a second なり.

jp: 疲[つか]れた時[とき]{は|wa-topic}、少[すこ]し休[やす]む{なり|nari-nari}早[はや]めに寝[ね]る{なり|nari-nari}しなさい。
en: When you are tired, either rest for a while or go to bed early.
why: Two verbs offered as alternatives, with the choice left to the listener, take Vなり Vなり before する.

jp: 暇[ひま]な日[ひ]{は|wa-topic}、本[ほん]{を|o-object}読[よ]む{なり|nari-nari}映画[えいが]{を|o-object}見[み]る{なり|nari-nari}して、ゆっくり過[す]ごしなさい。
en: On a free day, read a book or watch a film or something, and take it easy.
why: なり lists alternatives as suggestions: any one of them will do, and the second なり, followed by して, completes the pair.

jp: 道[みち]{が|ga-subject}分[わ]からなかっ{たら|tara-conditional}、駅員[えきいん]さん{に|ni-target}尋[たず]ねる{なり|nari-nari}地図[ちず]{で|de-means}確認[かくにん]する{なり|nari-nari}しなさい。
en: If you don't know the way, either ask a station attendant or check it on a map.
why: Two possible actions offered as advice are linked as Vなり Vなり, and する follows the second なり.

jp: 詳[くわ]しいこと{は|wa-topic}、案内所[あんないじょ]{で|de-place}尋[たず]ねる{なり|nari-nari}ホームページ{を|o-object}見[み]る{なり|nari-nari}しなさい。
en: For the details, either ask at the information desk or look at the website.
why: Aなり Bなり presents two ways of doing something; the second なり must repeat the first.

jp: 辞書[じしょ]{を|o-object}引[ひ]く{なり|nari-nari}ネット{で|de-means}調[しら]べる{なり|nari-nari}して、意味[いみ]{を|o-object}確[たし]かめなさい。
en: Look it up in a dictionary or search online, and check the meaning.
why: Whichever way the listener chooses, the two means are offered as Aなり Bなり, followed by して.

jp: 嫌[いや]なこと{は|wa-topic}、断[ことわ]る{なり|nari-nari}逃[に]げる{なり|nari-nari}すればいい。
en: If something is unpleasant, you can just turn it down or get away from it.
why: Two alternative actions each get なり, and する (すれば) follows the second one.

jp: 荷物[にもつ]{は|wa-topic}、宅配便[たくはいびん]{なり|nari-nari}郵便[ゆうびん]{なり|nari-nari}{で|de-means}送[おく]りなさい。
en: Send the luggage by courier or by post, whichever you like.
why: Nouns can also be paired: 宅配便なり郵便なり means either courier or post, your choice.

jp: 日曜日[にちようび]{は|wa-topic}、散歩[さんぽ]{なり|nari-nari}買[か]い物[もの]{なり|nari-nari}、好[す]きなこと{を|o-object}しなさい。
en: On Sunday, go for a walk or go shopping, or do whatever you like.
why: 散歩なり買い物なり offers two sample activities with the choice left open; the second なり is required.

jp: 困[こま]った時[とき]{は|wa-topic}、警察[けいさつ]{なり|nari-nari}役所[やくしょ]{なり|nari-nari}{に|ni-target}相談[そうだん]しましょう。
en: When you are in trouble, let's consult either the police or the town office.
why: The pair Aなり Bなり can be followed by a particle such as に that applies to both nouns.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}何[なに]か言[い]う{なり|nari-nari}怒[おこ]る{なり|nari-nari}する{と|to-quote}思[おも]った{が|ga-but}、黙[だま]ったままだった。
en: I thought he would either say something or get angry, but he just stayed silent.
why: Vなり Vなり lists two expected reactions as alternatives, then する follows the second なり.

jp: 駅[えき]{から|kara-from}ホテル{まで|made-until}、バス{なり|nari-nari}タクシー{なり|nari-nari}{で|de-means}行[い]けます。
en: From the station to the hotel, you can go by bus or by taxi.
why: Two means of transport offered as options are paired with なり, and で follows the pair.

jp: 遊[あそ]ぶ前[まえ]{に|maeni-atode}、部屋[へや]{を|o-object}掃除[そうじ]する{なり|nari-nari}宿題[しゅくだい]{を|o-object}済[す]ませる{なり|nari-nari}しなさい。
en: Before you play, either clean your room or finish your homework.
why: Aなり Bなり gives two acceptable tasks, and the second なり must match the first.

jp: 気[き]に入[い]らない物[もの]{は|wa-topic}、返品[へんぴん]する{なり|nari-nari}交換[こうかん]する{なり|nari-nari}、ご自由[じゆう]にどうぞ。
en: If you don't like something, feel free to return it or exchange it, as you wish.
why: なり…なり leaves the choice between two actions entirely to the listener.

jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]す前[まえ]{に|maeni-atode}、役所[やくしょ]{で|de-place}手続[てつづ]き{を|o-object}する{なり|nari-nari}大家[おおや]さん{に|ni-target}連絡[れんらく]する{なり|nari-nari}すべきだった。
en: Before moving, you should have either done the paperwork at the town office or contacted the landlord.
why: Two things one could have done are joined as Vなり Vなり, and する follows the pair.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]み{は|wa-topic}、海[うみ]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]く{なり|nari-nari}旅行[りょこう]する{なり|nari-nari}して、思[おも]い切[き]り楽[たの]しんでください。
en: In the summer holidays, go to the seaside or take a trip or something, and enjoy yourself to the full.
why: Two sample activities offered as suggestions take なり after each verb, and して follows the pair.

jp: この問題[もんだい]{は|wa-topic}、先輩[せんぱい]{に|ni-target}聞[き]く{なり|nari-nari}本[ほん]{で|de-means}調[しら]べる{なり|nari-nari}する{しか|shika-nai}ない。
en: For this problem, we have no choice but to ask a senior or look it up in a book.
why: Two possible remedies are listed with なり…なり, and する closes the pair.

jp: 返事[へんじ]{は|wa-topic}メール{なり|nari-nari}電話[でんわ]{なり|nari-nari}、都合[つごう]{の/が|no-subject}いい方法[ほうほう]{で|de-means}構[かま]いません。
en: As for the reply, e-mail or phone is fine, whichever method suits you.
why: メールなり電話なり offers two accepted methods; the choice is the listener's.

jp: 寒[さむ]い日[ひ]{は|wa-topic}、上着[うわぎ]{を|o-object}着[き]る{なり|nari-nari}暖房[だんぼう]{を|o-object}つける{なり|nari-nari}しましょう。
en: On a cold day, let's either put on a jacket or turn on the heating.
why: Two ways of dealing with the cold are offered as options, each verb taking なり.
